transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-06
Start time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Greene (CSM), Alex Kim (Cypress Head of ML), Jamie Ortega (Product), Samir Patel (CTO), Rina Zhou (Data Engineer)

Summary:
- Weekly POC sync focused on scorecard regressions, guardrail tuning, and next steps for pilot scale tests.
- Reviewed recent drop in pass-rate on intent classification and a burst of hallucination in long-context prompts.
- Agreed to run larger regression with quantized variant and collect latency/cost breakdowns.
- Action owners assigned; follow-up deep-dive with infra requested.

Topics covered:
- Recent scorecard results (precision/recall by intent)
- Prompt set gap analysis and new negative examples
- Guardrail (regex + model-based) false positives and thresholds
- Deployment trade-offs: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
- Compliance asks: audit logs, KMS, SSO/SAML

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check - does the time still work for the cypress team?
[00:00:12] Alex: Yeah 14:30 is good, thanks. we've got Samir and Rina on as well, I'll hand it to Jamie to frame what we saw this week.
[00:00:20] Jamie: cool thanks. so in the dashboard we pushed v2 prompts and saw a drop in our high-confidence label pass-rate, about 12% down, and a few hallucination cases on the long context tickets.
[00:00:32] Priya: when you say long context, is that the 2.5k token threads or the concatenated history?
[00:00:37] Jamie: mostly the concatenated history. some of our e2e flows concatenate user comments, system metadata, and a chunk of doc text.
[00:00:44] Samir: just to add, infra noticed p95 latency spikes when we hit ~50 concurrent requests, and that lined up with the batch window where the KV cache warm start didn't help. 
[00:00:55] Rina: little note - some logs show 'k v cash' spelled out in our telemetry; hope that's just a transcription quirk, ha.
[00:01:02] Liam: (laughs) yeah I saw that in the export too. okay, Priya can you walk thru the scorecard? we had the report right?
[00:01:10] Priya: yep, I pulled today's run. high level: intent precision dropped from 0.89 to 0.77 on the prod prompt set, recall stayed similar. Most errors are false positives — model labeling a user question as "approve" when it's actually info-seeking.
[00:01:25] Priya: we ran two variants: baseline fp16, and a q4 quantized variant. q4 showed better steady-state latency but slightly worse precision on the same prompts. looks like quantization pushed some decision boundaries.
[00:01:40] Alex: that's the tradeoff we were worried about. cost is attractive on q4 though — token cost down ~35%.
[00:01:46] Jamie: do we have per-route latency breakdown? the dashboard shows P50/P95 but not split by prompt length.
[00:01:53] Priya: I have a CSV I'll share — includes latency by token count bucket (<=256, 257-1024, >1024). p95 for >1024 was the problematic one.
[00:02:02] Liam: can you highlight the 10 worst failures and the prompts that trigger them? that'll help narrow guardrail adjustments.
[00:02:08] Priya: yes, already flagged 12 examples in the report. most are prompt engineering issues — we have leading context that biases output.
[00:02:14] Alex: so next step is to add negative examples and test. but also we'd like to try Redwood's model-based guardrail, right? you mentioned a classifier layer.
[00:02:22] Priya: right — Redwood offers a lightweight reranker/classifier you can run post-gen to filter outputs. it's a small model that scores safety and relevance; we've seen it cut hallucination by ~40% in other pilots.
[00:02:33] Jamie: does that add a lot of latency?
[00:02:35] Priya: marginal. it's usually microseconds to low tens of ms depending on whether it's colocated or separate. If you colocate on the same pod we can keep the end-to-end p95 in a target band.
[00:02:45] Samir: we need to know about resource footprint — can that run on our dedicated pool? we want to avoid a second GPU for a tiny model.
[00:02:52] Priya: the reranker is CPU-friendly and can run on CPU nodes for small throughput. for higher throughput we recommend a small GPU or sharing a GPU with quantized variants. I'll include sample memory/CPU numbers in the follow-up.
[00:03:02] Liam: good. on the compliance side Jamie asked about audit logs and key management?
[00:03:07] Maya: we have a SOC2 pack and a KMS integration doc. Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Private deployments and can integrate with AWS KMS/HSM. For Hosted we offer encrypted at rest with Redwoods-managed keys by default, but we can scope a dedicated KMS for enterprise pilots.
[00:03:22] Alex: we will need customer-managed KMS for the pilot and SSO - SAML. can we get those docs?
[00:03:28] Maya: yes I'll drop the compliance packet and SSO setup guide after the call.
[00:03:32] Rina: for benchmarking we'd like an SSO test account and API keys that allow us to push load from our infra.
[00:03:38] Liam: noted — Rina you'll get a service account and a staging key. Priya will run the regression with your prompt sets.
[00:03:44] Priya: quick question about scoring: Cypress's current scorecard weights precision over recall 70/30, is that correct?
[00:03:51] Alex: yes, because false approvals cost us more. but with the uptick in false positives we might shift to 60/40 temporarily while we tune guardrails.
[00:03:59] Priya: okay we'll run both thresholds and compare expected business impact in the report.
[00:04:05] Liam: can we also capture token-level cost and show delta between baseline and q4 quantized?
[00:04:09] Priya: yes — cost per 1k tokens, and projected monthly spend based on current traffic are in the CSV.
[00:04:14] Jamie: one more ask — our product team wants to see a short list of prompt edits to attempt before model changes, like template tightening and explicit cast of intent.
[00:04:21] Priya: we have 8 suggested prompt rewrites in the doc. some are small (explicit instruction to not infer intent from system metadata), others are structural. We'll A/B them internally.
[00:04:29] Alex: good. how about regression cadence — how long do you need to run a reliable check?
[00:04:33] Priya: for 2k prompts it's about 3-4 hours with our current test harness on a single GPU; parallelized across 2 GPUs it's under 2 hours. I'll estimate time in the ticket.
[00:04:43] Samir: for benchmarking we want to run with our own load generator to see network effects. can we coordinate an infra session?
[00:04:48] Liam: yes we'll set a deep-dive. Samir, what's your availability week of the 13th?
[00:04:54] Samir: Tue/Thu afternoon PST works best.
[00:04:57] Liam: perfect we'll schedule that.
[00:05:00] [00:05:00 - 00:25:00 condensed transcript of technical walk-through where Priya shared the CSV and they reviewed 12 failure cases one-by-one; transcription includes partial overlaps and mislabeling]
[00:25:12] Priya: first failure — prompt id 2345, model returns an approval token in presence of negation. you can see the original user text: 'I don't want to proceed' but system metadata had 'urgent: true' — model prioritized system tag.
[00:25:27] Jamie: that's a prompt bug. we can demote system tags or change the cueing.
[00:25:31] Alex: agreed, we'll adjust. also can we add a simple regex-based block for outputs containing 'I approve' when the input has negative polarity?
[00:25:40] Priya: yes but regex can introduce false negatives — we'll prototype a hybrid: regex + model-based reranker with threshold.
[00:25:48] Liam: please capture the exact regex candidate and we'll review.
[00:25:51] Priya: noted.
[00:26:05] [small crosstalk and typing noises]
[00:26:22] Speaker 3: just to flag, a few of our passed examples look like edge cases where entity extraction failed and that cascaded to wrong intent.
[00:26:31] Rina: yeah some of our entity parsers are brittle. we can add more annotated entities to the dataset.
[00:26:36] Priya: that will help. also we'll add a few synthetic negative examples.
[00:26:42] Alex: when you run the q4 regression can you also include the baseline fp16 and the hosted Redwood model so we can compare three ways?
[00:26:50] Priya: absolutely — baseline (fp16), q4 quant, plus hosted benchmark should be in the output.
[00:26:56] Jamie: fine. on the guardrail side, we want to avoid over-blocking live traffic. what's your recommended fail-open policy?
[00:27:03] Priya: recommended pattern: soft-fail on low-confidence block (log + temp hold), hard-fail on high-confidence safety flags. Also add human-in-loop for 'sensitive' category until threshold drops.
[00:27:14] Alex: okay we'll run soft-fail for 48 hours then evaluate.
[00:27:18] Liam: quick commercial note — given the expected scale, we should discuss Dedicated pricing as a potential cost-saver once you hit steady-state. I'll put pricing tiers in the sheet.
[00:27:27] Samir: make sure the pricing includes burst capacity and SLA for p95.
[00:27:31] Liam: will do.
[00:27:35] [00:27:35 - 00:43:00 quick Q&A and clarifications about CSV columns, metric definitions, and a request for a canonical 'failure-case template' to use for triage]
[00:43:08] Jamie: one last item — can Redwood provide a simple script to compute the scorecard metric locally so we can run iterations without hitting the staging endpoint?
[00:43:16] Priya: yes we have a scoring harness we'll share; it's a small python script that ingests a CSV and outputs precision/recall/confusion matrix.
[00:43:24] Alex: perfect.
[00:43:28] Liam: recap and next steps — Priya runs the 2k regression (baseline, q4, hosted), Priya shares CSV and latency/cost breakdown; Liam sends pricing and pilot amendment; Maya shares SOC2/KMS/SSO docs; Alex shares prompts and failure flags; schedule infra deep-dive w/ Samir for week of 10/13.
[00:43:46] Maya: I'll email the compliance pack and SSO guide within 24 hours.
[00:43:50] Rina: I'll provision the SSO test account and share credentials via secure vault.
[00:43:55] Liam: thanks everyone — we'll reconvene next week same time.
[00:44:00] Alex: thanks all.

End of transcript.
